c.tagline: Sun-drenched Ceará capital of Beira Mar, forró nights, and Praia do Futuro.

taxi.fareNote: City taxis are metered; ride-hailing apps (Uber, 99) are widely used and usually cheaper than street taxis.

emergency.note: 193 reaches the fire brigade; 190 is the military police; 192 summons SAMU ambulances.

avoid.reason: Elevated violent crime; caution on Praia de Iracema seafront at night and peripheral areas

hood_desc: Fortaleza's prime beachfront district along Avenida Beira Mar, with a wide seaside promenade, the nightly craft fair, hotels, restaurants and beach kiosks; the safest, most central base for most visitors.

The beach neighborhood closest to downtown, home to the Ponte dos Ingleses pier, the Centro Dragão do Mar cultural complex and the city's liveliest bar-and-club nightlife strip; walkable to the center.
The eastern continuation of Beira Mar ending at a working fishing colony and the Mercado dos Peixes, quieter and known for sunrise views over the jangada sailboats; a calmer seaside stay.
An upscale residential district just inland from the beach, packed with shopping malls, shops, restaurants and hospitals; a convenient, safe base a short ride from the sand.
A long, open-sea beach lined with large barracas (beach clubs) famous for fried fish, crab nights and weekend live music; a lively beach-day and nightlife destination away from the hotel strip.

transit.pay: Buses and BRT use the rechargeable Bilhete Único card or cash to the driver (about R$4.50 a ride, with free transfers within two hours on the card); the VLT light rail uses its own low-fare ticket.
transit.hours: City buses and BRT run roughly 5am to midnight; the VLT Parangaba–Mucuripe light rail runs a more limited daytime schedule.
transit.note: Fortaleza's public transport is a large municipal bus network (Topbus+) with BRT corridors, plus the VLT Parangaba–Mucuripe light-rail line linking inland train districts to the port; the Beira Mar beachfront itself is very walkable.

transit.m: Topbus+ / municipal bus to Beira Mar and center (~40 min)
Taxi or ride-hail to Beira Mar (15-25 min)

tip.r: A 10% service charge is usually already added to restaurant bills; extra tipping is optional.

food.name: Caranguejo (mangrove crab)
food.desc: Whole mangrove crabs boiled in coconut milk and coriander broth, cracked open with a wooden mallet - Fortaleza's beach ritual, best on Thursdays.

places.name: Chico do Caranguejo
places.note: The name in crab on Praia do Futuro; Thursday crab nights with live forro and comedy draw big local crowds.

places.name: Crocobeach
places.note: Largest of the beachfront barracas; crab platters, pools and sunset music, reliably busy year-round.

places.name: Mercado dos Peixes
places.note: Buy crab and fish at the stalls and have the cooks fry or boil it on the spot for a few reais.

food.name: Peixe na telha
food.desc: Fillet of red snapper or pescada baked on a clay roof tile with tomato, onion, peppers and coconut milk, served bubbling at the table.

places.name: Colher de Pau
places.note: Long-running Cearense kitchen locals send visitors to for regional fish and seafood classics.

places.name: Coco Bambu Beira Mar
places.note: The chain was born in Fortaleza; enormous sharing plates of fish and shrimp on the seafront strip.

places.name: Terra do Sol
places.note: The barraca people pick when the meal matters more than the loungers; strong grilled and baked fish.

food.name: Baiao de dois
food.desc: The sertao staple: rice and green beans cooked together with coalho cheese, cream and often carne de sol crumbled through it.

places.name: Cabana do Sol
places.note: Institution for sertao cooking; the baiao de dois and carne de sol combo is what regulars order.

places.name: Colher de Pau
places.note: Homestyle Ceara plates with baiao de dois as the default side; good value set lunches.

places.name: Delicias do Ceara
places.note: Simple, well reviewed regional canteen serving the classic northeastern combination plates.

food.name: Carne de sol com macaxeira
food.desc: Sun-cured beef grilled and sliced, piled with buttery cassava, coalho cheese and vinaigrette - the inland dish every Fortaleza table shares.

places.name: Cabana do Sol
places.note: Best known carne de sol house in the city, generous sharing portions and a fixture for decades.

places.name: Mercado Central de Fortaleza
places.note: Upper-floor food stalls sell carne de sol plates alongside the cashew and cachaca shops.

places.name: Camarada Camarao
places.note: Ceara-founded seafood chain that also does a solid carne de sol; easy, air-conditioned option.

food.name: Tapioca
food.desc: Cassava-starch crepe cooked dry on a hot plate and folded over coalho cheese, coconut, carne de sol or condensed milk - breakfast and late-night alike.

places.name: Casario das Tapioqueiras
places.note: A whole row of tapioca huts on the highway out of town; the classic Ceara tapioca pilgrimage.

places.name: Feirinha da Beira Mar
places.note: Evening seafront craft market with tapioca griddles working until late beside the food stalls.

places.name: Mercado Central de Fortaleza
places.note: Reliable daytime tapioca counters for a cheap cheese-and-coconut version while shopping.

food.name: Peixada cearense
food.desc: Ceara's own fish stew - firm white fish simmered with potato, carrot, egg and coriander in a light coconut broth, ladled over rice and pirao.

places.name: Mercado dos Peixes
places.note: Pick the fish off the ice and the stall kitchens turn it into peixada; as fresh as it gets in the city.

places.name: Coco Bambu Beira Mar
places.note: Huge, dependable seafood portions on the beachfront; a safe first-night introduction to local fish.

places.name: Colher de Pau
places.note: Traditional Cearense recipes cooked to order, including the classic peixada with pirao.

food.name: Agua de coco
food.desc: Chilled green coconut water drunk straight from the shell with a straw, sold from carts and barracas the length of the beachfront.

places.name: Beira Mar boardwalk carts
places.note: Dozens of licensed coconut carts along the promenade; freshly hacked open in front of you.

places.name: Crocobeach
places.note: Beach club service brings whole iced coconuts to your lounger all day.

places.name: Praia de Iracema kiosks
places.note: Sunset spot where locals stop for coconut water before the bars open.

food.name: Cajuina and cashew juice
food.desc: Cajuina is a clarified, caramel-coloured sparkling cashew-apple juice; the fresh suco de caju version is tarter and served over ice.

places.name: Mercado Central de Fortaleza
places.note: Bottled cajuina and cashew products sold across the market alongside juice counters.

places.name: Feirinha da Beira Mar
places.note: Juice stalls press caju, cajá, acerola and graviola to order in the evening market.

places.name: Colher de Pau
places.note: Regional fruit juice list that runs well beyond the usual, cajuina included.

landmarks: Avenida Beira Mar
Fortaleza's signature oceanfront boulevard, a palm-lined promenade of joggers, coconut stands and a nightly handicraft fair beside Meireles beach.
Praia de Iracema and Ponte dos Ingleses
The city's bohemian beach quarter, where the early-1900s English Pier juts into the surf for sunsets and dolphin spotting.
Centro Dragão do Mar de Arte e Cultura
A striking cultural complex of museums, cinemas and a planetarium, its elevated walkways linking restored pastel-colored warehouses full of nightlife.
Theatro José de Alencar
A 1910 architectural jewel combining cast-iron Art Nouveau galleries imported from Scotland with a lush interior garden and eclectic facade.
Mercado Central de Fortaleza
A four-story hive of more than 500 stalls selling cashews, lacework, leather and cachaça, the classic stop for Ceará souvenirs.
Catedral Metropolitana de Fortaleza
An imposing neo-Gothic cathedral inspired by Cologne's, seating 5,000 beneath twin 75-meter towers and vivid stained glass.
Praia do Futuro
The city's best swimming beach, a long Atlantic strand famous for its barracas, giant beach clubs serving fried fish and crab feasts.
Fortaleza de Nossa Senhora da Assunção
The 17th-century Dutch-founded fort that gave the city its name, still an army base with guided visits and harbor views.
Mucuripe Fish Market and Jangadas
The traditional fishing corner of Beira Mar where triangular-sailed jangada rafts land the dawn catch immortalized in Brazilian song.
Cumbuco Beach
A world-renowned kitesurfing village of dunes, lagoons and buggy rides half an hour west of the city.

train.note: No intercity passenger rail. Fortaleza has the Metrofor light-rail and metro system covering the city and nearby towns, but nothing that leaves the state. Long-distance travel is by coach or plane.

bus.note: No international coaches. The Rodoviária Engenheiro João Thomé is south of the centre, with Guanabara, Expresso Guanabara and Itapemirim-successor operators running to Natal (about 8 hours), Recife (12), São Luís (18) and Teresina; book through ClickBus (https://www.clickbus.com.br/). Jericoacoara is reached by bus plus a 4x4 transfer over the dunes.

ferry.note: There is no scheduled passenger ferry from Fortaleza. The Mucuripe port is a commercial and cruise harbour, and the boats from the Praia de Iracema jetty are sunset and sightseeing cruises rather than transport.

half.name: Canoa Quebrada
half.blurb: Bohemian beach village on red-orange sandstone cliffs, long popular for its dunes, buggy rides, and laid-back nightlife.

half.name: Morro Branco & Beberibe Cliffs
half.blurb: Striped, multicolored sandstone cliffs along the coast southeast of Fortaleza, framing a quiet fishing beach below.

half.name: Lagoinha Beach
half.blurb: Palm-lined beach town with a freshwater lagoon behind the dunes, reached along the scenic Rota das Emoções coastal road.
